rationale: CHARACTERIZATION fixture, deliberately GREEN on arrival: it pins behaviour that already worked, because the change it guards is a REFACTOR, not a fix. `parseVForDirective` replaced `/^\s*\(?([^)]*?)\)?\s+(?:in|of)\s+(.+)$/` and its tail-less sibling so the Vue analyzer could reach ZERO regex literals, and three of the old pattern's behaviours are subtle enough to regress silently: (1) the alias head is the SHORTEST run without a `)`, so a greedy parser binds `row, i in grid` as one name; (2) the `)` belongs to the keyword match, not the head, so `(row, i) in grid` must bind TWO names; (3) `.` does not match a newline, so `v-for="multiline in\n spread"` fails the collection form and the caller falls back to the whole directive — visible here because `spread` is still found while the shadowing of `multiline` is unaffected. `of` is pinned alongside `in` because they are alternatives in the same group, and the destructuring slot prop `{ scoped, other: renamed }` pins the shared identifier tokenizer (F14-era) rather than a second one. Equivalence with the removed patterns is proved separately over 799 generated shapes (script/m60/verify-vue-no-regex.ts) and end-to-end over all 1,139 corpus files, both byte-for-byte; this fixture is what keeps the property true as the code is edited from here on.
